title: UWB Without the Integration Headache: Ceva and LG Bring Precision to More Chips - Semiwiki
gist: Ceva and LG Electronics' SoC Center have paired Ceva-Waves UWB baseband IP and software with an LG RF front end targeted at TSMC's 22-nanometer process, creating a pre-validated, licensable radio-to-software UWB platform supporting the emerging IEEE 802.15.4ab standard. The aim is to convert UWB from a specialist integration project into a drop-in SoC building block for automotive, industrial and consumer chips — with a major U.S. semiconductor supplier already signed and ABI Research forecasting UWB device shipments rising from 597 million in 2026 to nearly 1.18 billion by 2030.

insights.claim: Ceva and LG Electronics have combined Ceva-Waves UWB baseband intellectual property and software with an RF front end developed by LG Electronics' SoC Center into a single joint platform.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: LG monetising internal SoC Center RF expertise through an IP partner is a new revenue path for consumer OEMs with captive design teams.
insights.quote: Their joint platform combines Ceva-Waves UWB baseband intellectual property and software with an RF front end developed by LG Electronics’ SoC Center.
insights.locator: Key takeaways — Ceva and LG Electronics have joined forces

insights.claim: The RF front end is designed specifically for TSMC's 22-nanometer process, giving semiconductor companies a silicon-ready route to add precise ranging, positioning and sensing.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Process-specific hardening is what converts IP into a schedule guarantee — and it concentrates the design win on TSMC 22nm capacity.
insights.quote: The RF is designed for TSMC’s 22-nanometer process, giving semiconductor companies a silicon-ready route
insights.locator: Key takeaways — Their joint platform combines

insights.claim: The division of labour is that LG supplies analog and RF circuitry generating and receiving extremely short wide-spectrum pulses while Ceva supplies the digital baseband that converts those signals into timing and distance information plus the configuration software.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Clean RF/digital split explains why neither firm could serve this market alone — analog RF expertise is the scarce input in UWB.
insights.locator: Technically, the partnership closes the gap between two tightly coupled parts

insights.claim: Packaging RF and baseband as a coordinated solution should reduce interface validation, physical-design work and performance tuning compared with sourcing radio and baseband separately.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Integration cost, not licence price, is the real barrier being removed — the value proposition is schedule and respin risk, not silicon area.
insights.locator: Packaging those elements as a coordinated solution

themes.theme: Why UWB integration is genuinely hard

insights.claim: UWB performance depends on far more than protocol-compliance checkboxes: accurate ranging requires precise timestamping, synchronization and channel estimation while coping with interference, multipath reflections and non-line-of-sight conditions.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Explains why UWB adoption has lagged its standard — certification does not guarantee usable accuracy, so pre-validated silicon carries real premium value.
insights.quote: Accurate ranging requires precise timestamping, synchronization and channel estimation while coping with interference, multipath reflections and non-line-of-sight conditions.
insights.locator: That matters because UWB performance depends on more than checking protocol-compliance boxes

insights.claim: Power consumption and silicon area must remain low enough for battery-powered tags, phones, wearables and embedded controllers, constraining how much performance an implementation can buy.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: The power/area budget caps UWB's reach into the highest-volume battery devices — the constraint that decides whether the 1.18bn forecast lands.
insights.locator: Power consumption and silicon area must also remain low enough

insights.claim: An RF and baseband designed and validated together gives SoC developers a more predictable path through these trade-offs, shortening development cycles and lowering the risk of expensive silicon respins.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Respin avoidance is quantifiable in dollars and months — the metric a chipmaker uses to justify paying for bundled IP over best-of-breed sourcing.
insights.locator: An RF and baseband designed and validated together

themes.theme: 802.15.4ab and the expansion of UWB capability

insights.claim: Ceva's next-generation architecture supports IEEE 802.15.4ab, the emerging evolution of the UWB standard, which improves extended-range and non-line-of-sight ranging, adds interference resilience, supports new channels and enables UWB radar sensing.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Radar sensing added to a ranging standard expands the addressable use cases well beyond keys and trackers — watch for UWB displacing dedicated sensors.
insights.quote: it improves extended-range and non-line-of-sight ranging, adds resilience to interference, supports new channels and enables UWB radar sensing
insights.locator: Ceva’s next-generation architecture supports IEEE 802.15.4ab

insights.claim: These additions push UWB beyond its familiar roles in phone-assisted item finding and vehicle digital keys toward estimating position, direction and movement with high precision.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Broadening from binary presence detection to continuous spatial tracking is what would take UWB attach rates from niche to mainstream.
insights.quote: Instead of merely detecting whether a credential is nearby, systems can estimate position, direction and movement with high precision
insights.locator: Those additions push UWB beyond its familiar roles

insights.claim: Time-of-flight measurement helps UWB resist relay attacks that can fool technologies relying mainly on received signal strength, giving it a structural security advantage over RSSI-based proximity systems.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Security, not convenience, is the argument that forces automotive OEMs off Bluetooth-based keyless entry — a regulatory and insurance-driven adoption path.
insights.quote: time-of-flight measurements help resist relay attacks that can fool technologies based mainly on received signal strength
insights.locator: Instead of merely detecting whether a credential is nearby

themes.theme: Three end markets and the licensing business model

insights.claim: In vehicles UWB can support secure passive entry, occupant detection, child-presence monitoring, automated parking interactions and precise location of devices inside or around the cabin.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Child-presence detection is becoming a regulated safety feature in several markets, which would make UWB attach mandatory rather than optional in cars.
insights.locator: The market implications span three large semiconductor categories

insights.claim: In factories and warehouses UWB can track tools, pallets, robots and personnel, improve geofencing and support safer human-machine collaboration where ordinary Bluetooth proximity is too ambiguous.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Industrial safety zoning around robots is a compliance-driven budget line that tolerates higher BOM cost than consumer — likely the earliest profitable volume.
insights.quote: where ordinary Bluetooth proximity is too ambiguous
insights.locator: In factories and warehouses

insights.claim: In consumer products UWB can enable spatially aware smart-home controls, indoor navigation, peer-to-peer discovery, access systems and gesture or presence sensing without relying on a camera.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Camera-free presence sensing sidesteps privacy objections that have limited smart-home sensing — a differentiator versus vision-based approaches.
insights.quote: gesture or presence sensing without relying on a camera
insights.locator: In consumer products

insights.claim: Ceva licenses connectivity IP rather than selling a fixed chip, letting customers embed UWB inside a differentiated SoC alongside processors, security engines and other radios instead of depending on a standalone transceiver.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: IP licensing attacks the incumbent standalone-transceiver vendors by removing a chip from the BOM — a structural share shift, not a performance fight.
insights.quote: Ceva licenses connectivity IP rather than selling a fixed chip
insights.locator: The business model is equally important

insights.claim: A major U.S. semiconductor supplier has already adopted the combined Ceva-LG solution, providing early commercial validation of the platform.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: An unnamed lead customer is soft evidence — the named design win, when disclosed, is the catalyst to watch for Ceva licensing revenue.
insights.quote: The companies say a major U.S. semiconductor supplier has already adopted the combined solution
insights.locator: The business model is equally important

insights.claim: The approach could broaden the UWB supplier base because more chipmakers can build UWB products without assembling every layer internally or depending on a standalone transceiver.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: More suppliers means price competition in UWB silicon — margin pressure for existing transceiver vendors even as volumes grow.
insights.locator: This approach could broaden the supplier base

themes.theme: Adoption frictions and the volume forecast

insights.claim: Customers still have to complete system-level certification, antenna design, coexistence engineering, security architecture and interoperability testing themselves, so the integration burden is reduced rather than eliminated.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Tempers the 'drop-in block' pitch — time-to-market gains will be smaller than the marketing implies, so watch actual design-win-to-shipment lags.
insights.quote: Customers must complete system-level certification, antenna design, coexistence engineering, security architecture and interoperability testing.
insights.locator: There are still practical constraints

insights.claim: Support for 22nm suits cost-sensitive mixed-signal devices, but customers on other process nodes may require additional porting work, limiting the platform's immediate reach.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Node lock-in caps the near-term serviceable market to 22nm designs — porting cost is the gate on how fast this platform proliferates.
insights.quote: Support for 22nm is attractive for cost-sensitive mixed-signal devices, but customers using other process nodes may require additional porting.
insights.locator: There are still practical constraints

insights.claim: Adoption will hinge on consistent behaviour across phones, vehicles, access points and infrastructure rather than on excellent radio specifications alone.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: UWB is an ecosystem play with network effects — handset support is the gating dependency for every other category's business case.
insights.quote: Adoption will also depend on consistent behavior across phones, vehicles, access points and infrastructure, not simply excellent radio specifications.
insights.locator: There are still practical constraints

insights.claim: ABI Research, cited by Ceva, expects annual UWB device shipments to rise from 597 million in 2026 to nearly 1.18 billion by 2030, roughly a doubling in four years.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A ~19% CAGR unit forecast sets the revenue pool for UWB IP and silicon — note it is a vendor-cited number and should be treated as an upper bound.
insights.quote: ABI Research, cited by Ceva, expects annual UWB device shipments to rise from 597 million in 2026 to nearly 1.18 billion by 2030.
insights.locator: Bottom line

insights.claim: Putting standards-based UWB capability into many more product categories could itself improve interoperability, creating a reinforcing loop between scale and usability.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Identifies the network-effect flywheel that would make UWB forecasts self-fulfilling — or leave them stranded if the installed base stalls.
insights.quote: That scale could improve interoperability by putting standards-based capabilities into more product categories.
insights.locator: Bottom line
